# Dawid Szymanowski

> Dawid Szymanowski is a geochemist and geochronologist at ETH Zürich, where he has been an established researcher (Oberassistent) in the Institute of Geochemistry and Petrology since 2022. His work focuses on constraining the dates and rates of geological processes, originally in the high-temperature realm of magma reservoirs, but increasingly across a variety of lower-temperature settings, geological problems, and locations around the world. His main tool is high-precision U–Pb geochronology by isotope dilution thermal ionisation mass spectrometry (ID-TIMS), and he manages a specialised laboratory at ETH Zürich dedicated to this technique.

Much of his research is directed towards developing a better understanding of magmatic systems, magmatic and hydrothermal ore deposits, and the geochemical tools that can help study these topics. He also spends considerable time on fundamental research aimed at pushing the analytical limits of geochronology, as well as developing and applying new mineral chronometers.
